title: Learning to Stop without Learning to Stop: Self-Supervised Confidence Training Improves Reasoning Efficiency
why_read: A clever result showing that training models to predict their own confidence indirectly makes reasoning chains shorter without explicitly optimizing for brevity.
analysis: This paper shows that fine-tuning reasoning LLMs to self-predict confidence at intermediate reasoning steps reduces generated tokens by up to 25% at equal accuracy, even though the training objective never mentions length or stopping. The mechanism is self-supervised, needs only 600 training examples, and works across several model families including Gemma, Qwen, and GPT-OSS. This is notable because it suggests token efficiency can emerge as a side effect of teaching models better self-assessment rather than requiring explicit length penalties or early-stopping heuristics. It's a genuinely useful and cheap technique for anyone running expensive chain-of-thought inference at scale.
